clue.text: Division's supporting pro footballers

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first, holding it up

parts.note: pro means in favour of, which is for
wards are divisions of a city or hospital; the 's is read as a plural

explanation.surface: A league division backs its professional players.
explanation.definitionFit: Forwards are attacking players in a football team, the strikers and wingers.

clue.text: The man covering record, a Beatles record!

indicators.note: in a down clue the upper piece lies over the lower one like a lid

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Some man has got hold of a disc, and it is a Beatles one.
explanation.definitionFit: Help! was a 1965 album and single by the Beatles.

clue.text: Organised detectives giving rank

parts.note: to organise something is to run it, past tense ran
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives

explanation.surface: Detectives ran an operation that gave someone a rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means foul-smelling, the same as spoiled, stale-tasting butter.

clue.text: Endless calamity over time creates horror

indicators.note: the shortened word lies over, covering, the letter for time
without its end, so the final letter of the synonym is lost

parts.note: a calamity is a disaster

explanation.surface: A never-ending disaster stretched across time breeds horror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts DISASTER to DISASTE, and 'over' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is strong dislike or aversion, close in sense to a feeling of horror.

clue.text: Associate fellow set up embracing bird

indicators.note: the outer word holds the bird within its arms

parts.note: to raise something is to set it up
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A fellow builds a structure around a bird and keeps company with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fraternise is to mix socially, which is to associate with people.

clue.text: Oddly deep patches?

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the following words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: Strangely deep areas of ground, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep patches of sea or ground are depths, the deepest parts.

clue.text: Expect warning shout before round when facing tee

indicators.note: the warning shout comes first, ahead of the remaining pieces

parts.note: fore is what a golfer shouts to warn others
round means about, and c (circa) is the abbreviation for about
as can mean when, as in as he arrived
the letter T is spelt tee

explanation.surface: A golfer anticipates calling out a warning before the round, while standing on the tee.
explanation.walkthrough: The golfing surface suggests 'round' is a round of golf, but it means 'about', giving C.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast is to predict, to expect something to happen in the future.

clue.text: Foreign national seen in boat on Ganges

indicators.note: the answer is visible within the run of the following words

explanation.surface: A foreigner is spotted in a boat on the Ganges river.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tongan is a citizen of Tonga, a Pacific kingdom, so a national of a foreign country.

clue.text: King returns backing one's country

indicators.note: the reversed king stands behind, backing up, the first piece

parts.note: one is I, with the 's giving S

indicators.note: the king's name is turned to read backwards

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A king comes back to support his country.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: Hands over change

indicators.note: over signals the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: paws are hands, informally

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders their loose cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another, a kind of change.

clue.text: Make up into cutest swirls

indicators.note: the letters swirl around into a new order

explanation.surface: Applying make-up in pretty, swirling patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: To constitute something is to form or compose it, to make it up.

clue.text: Army capturing enemy's leader rejoiced

indicators.note: the outer word takes in the letter like a prisoner

parts.note: an army can mean a huge number of people, a crowd

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers celebrated after taking the enemy commander.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast or exult loudly, so crowed is a synonym of rejoiced.

clue.text: Harvest we threshed containing nothing at all

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the zero inside them
threshing beats grain about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Farmhands thresh the crop, which turns out to hold no grain whatever.
explanation.walkthrough: The farming surface hides the anagram signal: 'threshed' beats the letters into WHATSEVER, and 'containing' holds the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatsoever is an emphatic word meaning at all, as in no doubt whatsoever.

clue.text: Sailor's accurately holding south in deep

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, with the 's giving S

indicators.note: the word for accurately grips the letter inside

parts.note: true means accurate, as in aim true

explanation.surface: A sailor steers precisely, keeping south while out in the deep sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstruse means hard to understand, profound, as a deep thought is.

clue.text: Rare stigma found by Church

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace, a scar
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An unusual mark of shame is discovered near a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce means in short supply, hard to find, which is rare.

clue.text: He's a card, performing in pantomimes

indicators.note: the letters perform, acting out a new arrangement

parts.note: the contraction gives the letters H, E and S

explanation.surface: A joker who acts in Christmas shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges HESACARD. The definition is the guessing game of acted clues, not the British Christmas stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades are mimed word-guessing games, so pantomimes in the sense of dumb shows.

clue.text: Lechery of French master

parts.note: de is French for of
sire is an old form of address for a lord or master

explanation.surface: A French master's lust.
explanation.definitionFit: Desire includes sexual appetite, so lechery is a strong form of it.

clue.text: Swallowed by clientele, vat originally provides lift

indicators.note: the answer is taken in by the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Customers drink from a vat, which gives them a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevator is the American word for a lift between floors of a building.

clue.text: Wild, spasmodic utterance when receiving shock therapy

indicators.note: the hiccup takes in the treatment inside it

parts.note: hic is the sound of a hiccup
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: A patient blurts out strange noises while undergoing electric shock treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic means frantically busy, chaotic, which is wild in the sense of frenzied.

clue.text: Use charm as prude corrupts sweetheart

indicators.note: the letters are corrupted, spoiled into a new order

parts.note: the heart, the central letter, of the word sweet

explanation.surface: A seducer's charm works on a prim person, leading the prude astray.
explanation.definitionFit: To persuade someone is to win them over, often by using charm.

clue.text: Free from former wife, not quite available

parts.note: an ex is a former wife

indicators.note: the word lacks its last letter, falling just short

parts.note: an empty seat or room is free, available

explanation.surface: Released from an ex-wife who is no longer quite on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Exempt means not subject to an obligation, free from it.

clue.text: He produces case of beer with container

indicators.note: the case, the outer letters, of the following word

parts.note: an ewer is a jug, a container

explanation.surface: A man makes a case of beer along with a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewer is one who makes beer, a producer.

clue.text: Side street is ample around journey's end

indicators.note: the broad word goes round the final letter

parts.note: ample means wide, broad

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A side road is wide enough near the end of a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A byroad is a minor road, a side street off a main route.

clue.text: Supporter's complaint about new player

indicators.note: the grumble goes about, around, the letter for new

parts.note: a beef is a complaint
a player on stage is an actor

explanation.surface: A fan grumbles about a newly signed player.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of the definition stands for 'is', joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor gives money or help, so is a patron or backer.

clue.text: Eat too much cold stuff

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
to stuff is to ram, push in

explanation.surface: Gorging on cold food.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to stuff oneself with food, overeat.

clue.text: Team starts to collapse, relinquishing every wicket

indicators.note: the starting letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A cricket team begins to collapse, losing wicket after wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a group working together, a team.

clue.text: Globe, Shakespeare played initially in this place

indicators.note: the initial letters of the following two words are taken

parts.note: here means in this place

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's plays were first staged at the Globe, right here.
explanation.walkthrough: The Globe was Shakespeare's London theatre; here the word is just a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A globe is a round body, a sphere.

clue.text: One watches over guy with Queen playing

parts.note: a guy is a man, a chap
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
on means playing, as in a show being on

explanation.surface: A man goes to see the band Queen in concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon accompanies and supervises a young person, keeping watch over them.
